description: Authors interactive magic square puzzles. Produces a square grid where students fill in missing integers so every row, column, and diagonal sums to the same magic number, with configurable grid size (3×3, 4×4, 5×5, ...), problem statement, pre-populated hint or fixed cells via `initializeGrid`, and toggleable per-cell feedback. Supports classical (1..n² each used once) and generalized (any integers) magic squares. Describe the magic number, grid size, and scaffolding — L0154 wraps it in a single `magicSquare(...)` program.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a classical 3×3 magic square with magic number 15, show feedback on, and pre-fill the center cell with 5.
example_prompts.notes: The canonical 3×3 Lo Shu case — names the magic number, classical-domain convention, and one scaffolded cell so the translator knows which cells are given vs. to-fill.

example_prompts.prompt: Build a 4×4 magic square with magic sum 34, no pre-filled cells, and the prompt 'Fill in all 16 cells using each number from 1 to 16 exactly once.'
example_prompts.notes: 4×4 classical case with explicit prompt; omitting `initializeGrid` keeps every cell open, making this a blank puzzle.

example_prompts.prompt: Generalized 3×3 magic square where every line sums to 21, with four hint cells given (r1c1=10, r1c3=4, r3c1=1, r3c3=7) and feedback enabled.
example_prompts.notes: Exercises the generalized-domain path (non-1..n² integers) plus a four-corner hint scaffold via `initializeGrid` — forces the translator to both set the sum and supply cells.

example_prompts.prompt: Magic square 3×3 with magic number 15 and the corners already filled in (2, 4, 6, 8) so students only place the remaining five numbers.
example_prompts.notes: Partial-reveal scaffold — four corner cells given; exercises `initializeGrid` with a corner pattern commonly used in instruction.

example_prompts.prompt: Worked-example magic square: 3×3 fully filled (2 7 6 / 9 5 1 / 4 3 8) with feedback on and the prompt 'Verify that every row, column, and diagonal sums to 15.'
example_prompts.notes: All nine cells pre-populated via `initializeGrid`; feedback on so the item reads as a demonstration / verification task, not a solve-it puzzle.

example_prompts.prompt: 5×5 magic square with magic sum 65, feedback off, and the instruction 'Submit when all 25 cells use 1–25 exactly once.'
example_prompts.notes: Larger classical case with summative-style feedback off; names the magic sum 65 explicitly so the translator doesn't compute it incorrectly from the grid size.
